rows.label: Concept
rows.text: **Escape velocity** is the minimum launch speed that lets a body leave a planet's gravitational field, reaching infinity with zero speed. Energy conservation between the surface and infinity, $\frac{1}{2}mv_e^2 - \frac{GMm}{R} = 0$, gives $v_e = \sqrt{2GM/R} = \sqrt{2gR}$ — independent of the projectile's mass and direction (NEB 2023, 5m).…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - ½mv_e² = GMm/R → v_e = √(2GM/R) = √(2gR) - Earth: v_e = 11.2 km/s - v_e = √2 · v_o

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: At altitude h, use r=R+h in v_e=√(2GM/r); do not reuse the surface radius in the general expression.  ·  The derivation assumes no air resistance, spherical symmetry, negligible external bodies and no continuing thrust after launch.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: The formula neglects air resistance, rotation, external bodies and continued thrust.  ·  Escape speed is not the practical rocket delta-v from the launch pad.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***NEB 2022 planet*** — g = 5 m/s², R = 6×10⁶ m → v_e = 7.75 km/s.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: **Orbital vs escape:** √(gR) = 7.9 km/s keeps you circling; √(2gR) = 11.2 km/s sets you free.  ·  **Mass of the projectile is irrelevant** — a proton and a rocket share the same escape speed.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Derive escape speed using energy conservation.  ·  Find ve for M=6.0×10²⁴ kg and R=6.0×10⁶ m.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Numerical (3m): Find the escape velocity from Mars (M = 6.4×10²³ kg, R = 3.4×10⁶ m).** — v_e = √(2GM/R) = √(2×6.67×10⁻¹¹×6.4×10²³/3.4×10⁶) = √(2.51×10⁷) = 5.0 km/s.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: 2023 asked the full 5m derivation — practise writing it from the energy equation.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Energy conservation is the whole derivation:** ½mv² = GMm/R — KE must pay the full binding energy.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: $v_e = \sqrt{2GM/R} = \sqrt{2gR}$; Earth: 11.2 km/s; Moon: 2.4 km/s.  ·  $v_e = \sqrt{2}\,v_o$; direction-independent (no atmosphere).

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: The Moon's low escape velocity (2.4 km/s) is why it cannot retain an atmosphere; Earth's 11.2 km/s holds nitrogen and oxygen.

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: Escape speed depends on the projectile's mass → B  ·  v_esc equals → B

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Speed That Leaves Throw a ball up and it returns; launch it fast enough and it never comes back. The boundary speed — the escape velocity — depends only on the planet's mass and radius, not on the projectile. It is the speed at which kinetic energy exactly cancels the gravitational binding.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts (NEB 2022, 2023) ### 2.1 Definition **Escape velocity** is the minimum velocity with which a body must be projected from a planet's surface so that it escapes the planet's gravitational field completely (reaches infinity with zero speed).…  ·  ## 3. Conceptual Relationships - **To Topic 30:** the derivation is pure energy conservation with $U = -GMm/r$. - **To Topic 33:** $v_e = \sqrt{2}v_o$ at the same radius. - **To atmospheres:** gas molecules with rms speed comparable to $v_e$ leak away over time — why the Moon (2.4 km/s) is airless and Earth (11.2 km/s) kept its air.…
